item.title: beacon.sh
item.description:
beacon.sh addresses a limit of coding agents: they start each session knowing little about the project. Beacon watches what the agent does, such as commands that work, mistakes it makes, and conventions it discovers, and stores them as notes the agent can use next time.

It works with popular coding agents and keeps the memory in files and a local store the developer can inspect and edit. Over time, that cuts repeated explanations and failed attempts.

item.title: DeepSeek Super-Agent
item.description:
Super-Agent explores what a team-facing coding agent could look like. Built on DeepSeek’s Harness runtime, it is tied to one GitHub repository and listens for requests from approved colleagues in Feishu, a workplace chat app. A teammate can ask it to investigate or change something, and it works on the code and reports back.

The prototype shows how a lab thinks about agents inside everyday collaboration tools instead of only in a developer’s terminal. Because it is a prototype, it focuses on demonstrating the design, not on a polished product with broad integrations, and it requires technical setup.

item.title: Best of AI
item.description: Best of AI is a directory for finding AI tools without wading through hype. It lists tools by what they do, across more than a hundred categories such as code assistants, image generation, and meeting assistants, and by who uses them, with profession pages for designers, developers, marketers, lawyers, teachers, and many others. Each tool has a page with a description, category, price tier, website, tags, and links to alternatives.
